request: Two consecutive dashboard requests can show the first request’s count on the second. For example, records A and B have statuses open and closed. With the same cache, requesting open and then closed after changing B to open still reports one closed record. Restore correct counts without losing caching for identical requests.
preserve: let writes=0; const cache=new Map(); const set=cache.set.bind(cache); cache.set=(...args)=>{writes++;return set(...args);}; const rows=[{id:'a',status:'open'}]; assert.equal(api.dashboardCount(rows,'open',cache),1); assert.equal(api.dashboardCount(rows,'open',cache),1); assert.equal(api.dashboardCount(rows,'closed',cache),0); assert.equal(writes,2);

request: An import report sometimes drops one customer’s row when two customers use identifiers with similar punctuation, such as 'acme/east' with '01' and 'acme' with 'east/01'. Fix the report. Repeated rows with the same customer and order should still keep the last value, in first-seen order.
preserve: const first={customer:'a',order:'1',total:10}; const second={customer:'b',order:'2',total:20}; const replacement={...first,total:30}; assert.deepEqual(api.importReport([first,second,replacement]),[replacement,second]); assert.deepEqual(api.importReport([]),[]);
